chapters.title: SQL & Product Metrics

missions.rationale: The audit calls SQL non-negotiable and puts Analytics at 6.5/10 — the joint-lowest score with the highest weight. Nothing else on this roadmap unblocks as much.

tasks.title: Complete the Mode Analytics SQL tutorial

subtasks.title: Work the Mode case studies with real data

tasks.title: Solve 50 interview-grade SQL questions

Build one dashboard from your own queries

missions.reflectionPrompt: Which SQL construct still makes you hesitate, and what will you drill this week to fix it?

missions.title: Build 5 KPI frameworks
missions.summary: Construct and defend complete metric trees for five products you know.
missions.rationale: Metrics sits at 6.8/10. The audit is explicit: your documentation is excellent but your metric thinking is not equally visible. A metric tree is the artefact that makes it visible.

tasks.title: Learn the metric-tree structure cold
tasks.description: This exact chain is quoted in the audit. Learn it as a checklist you can run in an interview without thinking.

One long-term effect you would watch for 12 months

tasks.title: Framework 2 — a B2B SaaS workflow tool (Linear or Asana)

Framework 4 — a consumer subscription (Spotify or Duolingo)

Habit / streak mechanic and its metric

tasks.title: Framework 5 — an AI product (a copilot of your choosing)

subtasks.title: Quality metric and how it is measured

missions.reflectionPrompt: Which of your five trees would collapse first under an interviewer's "why that north star?"

missions.title: Set the operating system up
missions.summary: Put the habits and instrumentation in place before the hard months arrive.
missions.rationale: The audit's biggest listed mistake is measuring progress by effort instead of observable results. This mission makes results observable from day one.

subtasks.title: Block the hours in a calendar, not in your head
Choose the two days that are non-negotiable
Decide what gets dropped when the week goes wrong

tasks.title: Quantify three outcomes from your current role

Find or estimate the number for each

Sanity-check each with someone who was there

tasks.title: Stand up the portfolio site shell

subtasks.title: About page with the positioning statement
Empty case-study template you will reuse six times

missions.reflectionPrompt: What did you plan this month that you did not do, and was the plan wrong or the week?

Five complete metric trees you can defend in an interview

subtasks.title: Note where the two tools disagree and why

tasks.title: Design an event taxonomy from scratch

What you deliberately do not track
Migration plan for an existing bad taxonomy

missions.reflectionPrompt: Could you answer a retention question live, in the tool, while someone watches?

missions.summary: Funnel analysis, retention, cohort analysis and metric recommendations, in public.

chapters.title: Experimentation

missions.title: Learn experimentation properly
missions.summary: Statistical foundations first, tooling second.
missions.rationale: Experimentation is 6.2/10 — the lowest score in the audit and described as a large gap. Top PMs discuss power and confidence intervals continuously.

tasks.title: Read Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments, parts I–II

subtasks.title: Take notes as decision rules, not summaries

tasks.title: Learn to compute power, sample size and MDE by hand

Minimum detectable effect from a fixed sample
Effect of baseline rate on required n

missions.reflectionPrompt: Can you explain a p-value to a sceptical engineer without hedging?

missions.title: Design 10 A/B test plans
missions.summary: Ten complete plans, each defensible under cross-examination.
missions.rationale: The audit's measurable output for month 3. Ten plans also become a portfolio artefact and a bank of interview answers.

subtasks.title: Primary metric and why it is the primary
Plan 7: notification cadence with a guardrail on unsubscribes
Plan 10: model swap with a quality guardrail
Find someone who runs experiments for a living
Get written critique on at least three plans
Revise and record what you got wrong

missions.reflectionPrompt: Which of the ten would you actually bet money on, and why that one?

missions.title: Run one real experiment
missions.summary: However small. The point is the write-up.
missions.rationale: Hands-on experimentation is a must-fix item. Reading about it does not close the gap.

tasks.title: Find and ship a real test at work

subtasks.title: Pre-register the hypothesis and decision rule

tasks.title: Analyse and write it up honestly

subtasks.title: Read the result against the pre-registered rule
State the confidence interval, not just the point estimate
Write what you would do differently

missions.reflectionPrompt: What did the data say that you did not expect?

targetOutcomes: Compute sample size and MDE by hand
One real experiment run and written up
